t1262.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Hudhalī, Abū ʿAlī al-Khallāl al-Ḥulwānī, resident of Mecca, as trustworthy, a memorizer with writings; of the eleventh generation, dying in 42.
as: Yaʿqūb ibn Shaybah, quoted by al-Mizzī
He was trustworthy, dependable and precise.
He did not critically assess transmitters.
كان عالما بالرجال، وكان لا يستعمل علمه.
He knew the transmitters but did not apply his knowledge.
أبو سلمة بن شبيب, quoted by al-Mizzī
His learning should be thrown in the latrine.
He was trustworthy and a master of memorization.
عبد الله بن أحمد بن حنبل, quoted by al-Mizzī
I did not see my father take him lightly.

t4193.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Jurayj al-Makkī as trustworthy, a jurist and virtuous, of the sixth generation, who practiced tadlīs and irsāl and died in the year 50 or after.
as: Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
ثقة في كل ماروى عنه من الكتاب
Reliable in everything transmitted from him out of his book.
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان ابن جريج صدوقا فإذا قال: حدثني"فهو سماع، وإذا قال: أخبرنا"أو"أخبرني"فهو قراءة، وإذا قال: قال"فهو شبه الريح
Ibn Jurayj was truthful. “He told me” indicates hearing, “he informed us” or “he informed me” indicates reading, and “he said” is insubstantial.
عطاء بن أبو رباح, quoted by al-Mizzī
سيد شباب أهل الحجاز ابن جريج
The leader of the youth of the Ḥijāz is Ibn Jurayj.
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān, quoted by al-Mizzī
وابن جريج أثبت من مالك في نافع
Ibn Jurayj is more reliable than Mālik on Nāfiʿ.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
عمرو بن دينار وابن جريج أثبت الناس في عطاء
ʿAmr ibn Dīnār and Ibn Jurayj are the most reliable of people on ʿAṭāʾ.
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān, quoted by al-Mizzī
كنا نسمي كتب ابن جريج كتب الأمانة
We used to call Ibn Jurayj's books the books of trust.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
إذا قال ابن جريج"قال فلان""وقال فلان" "وأخبرت"جاء بمناكير
When Ibn Jurayj says 'so-and-so said' or 'I was told', he brings unacceptable reports; when he says 'he told me' or 'I heard', that suffices.
أبو عبد الله, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان ابن جريج من أوعية العلم
Ibn Jurayj was one of the vessels of knowledge.
يزيد بن زريع, quoted by al-Mizzī
Ibn Jurayj was a carrier of rubbish (indiscriminate material).
Mālik ibn Anas, quoted by al-Mizzī
Ibn Jurayj was a night wood-gatherer (collecting indiscriminately).
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
مخلد بن الحسين, quoted by al-Mizzī
ما رأيت خلقا من خلق الله أصدق لهجة من ابن جريج
I have not seen any of God's creatures more truthful in speech than Ibn Jurayj.
He was reliable and a very prolific transmitter.

t942.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān al-Ḍubaʿī, Abū Sulaymān al-Baṣrī, as truthful and ascetic but with Shiʿi leanings, of the eighth generation, who died in 78 AH.
as: Truthful and ascetic, but he had Shiʿi leanings.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
There is no harm in him.
سليمان بن حرب, quoted by al-Mizzī
His hadith is not to be written.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
إنما كان يتشيع، وكان يحدث بأحاديث في فضل علي
He merely had Shīʿī leanings and narrated hadiths on ʿAlī's merits.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
ثقة، كان يحيى بن سعيد لا يكتب حديثه
Reliable; Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd did not write his hadith.
ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī, quoted by al-Mizzī
أكثر عن ثابت، وكتب مراسيل وفيها أحاديث مناكير، عن ثابت، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.
He transmitted extensively from Thābit and wrote disconnected narrations, including objectionable hadiths from Thābit from the Prophet.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī, quoted by al-Mizzī
رأيت عبد الرحمن بن مهدي لا ينبسط لحديث جعفر بن سليمان.
I saw ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī show little enthusiasm for Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān's hadith.
أحمد بن سنان, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان ثقة، وبه ضعف، وكان يتشيع
He was reliable, with some weakness, and had Shīʿī leanings.
فرأيته فاضلا حسن الهدي، فأخذت هذا عنه.
I found him virtuous and of good conduct, and adopted this from him.
ولجعفر حديث صالح، وروايات كثيرة، وهو حسن الحديث، وهو معروف بالتشيع، وجمع الرقائق
Jaʿfar has acceptable hadiths and many transmissions. He is good in hadith, is known for his Shiʿi views, and collected spiritually edifying reports.
It is said he was illiterate.
محمد بن أبو بكر المقدمي, quoted by al-Mizzī
ما أفسد جعفرا غيره يعني في التشيع.
Only ʿAbd al-Razzāq corrupted Jaʿfar, meaning with respect to Shiʿi views.
وكان ثقة وبه ضعف. وكان يتشيع.
He was trustworthy, with some weakness, and held Shiʿi views.
